prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas. Injury: concussion. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1344; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record. You can refer to me as the plaintiff.

Q: Understood. Let's start with the accident itself. Where were you when it happened?

A: I was driving north on a two-lane road in Conroe, Texas. It was a clear afternoon and traffic was light.

Q: Can you describe what you saw immediately before the collision?

A: A pickup truck crossed the center line coming toward me. I braked and turned slightly to the right, but it was too late to avoid contact. The impact was head-on, though I'd say it was not a high-speed crash. Both vehicles were moving slowly when they met.

Q: Did you lose consciousness at any point?

A: I don't think I fully blacked out, but I was dazed. I remember the airbag going off and my head snapping back and forward. For a while everything felt slow and foggy.

Q: When did you first seek medical attention?

A: A paramedic checked me at the scene, and I went to the emergency room later that same day because I had a headache that wouldn't go away and I felt nauseous.

Q: What were you told about your condition?

A: The doctor said I had a concussion. They told me to rest, avoid screens as much as I could, and stay out of strenuous activity.

Q: Have you followed up with any specialists since then?

A: Yes, I've seen a neurologist and I've been to physical therapy for my neck. The neurologist did a series of tests on my balance and memory.

Q: How has the concussion affected your daily routine?

A: It's hard to describe. I used to read a lot and work on spreadsheets all day at my job. Now I get tired quickly, and reading for more than a few minutes gives me a headache. I've had to ask my employer for modified duties, and I sometimes leave early.

Q: Are there any activities you've stopped doing?

A: I used to play in a recreational volleyball league on weekends. I haven't been able to play since the accident. I also stopped driving at night because the bright lights bother me.

Q: Do you have any symptoms today?

A: Some days are better than others. Bright light and loud noise still bother me, and I have occasional dizziness when I stand up too quickly. My family has noticed I'm more irritable than I used to be.

Q: Thank you. I have no further questions at this time.
